## Summary

I built a complete RS274/NGC G-code simulator at `output/main.py` (entry point) + `output/rs274/` (package), covering the full specification: all G-codes and M-codes, all 9 canned cycles (G81–G89) with sticky R/Z and repeat semantics, cutter radius compensation (entry moves, corner arcs, D0/zero-radius per the Clarification), G92/G10/G28/G30, tool table and parameter file I/O, G38.2 probing against a probe box, block-delete, and the full custom motion-trace engine (time/distance/tolerance-based stepping with delta-encoded entries).

**Validation:** all three worked trace examples in your spec matched byte-for-byte, and all three Appendix C sample programs (Hello World, expression torture test, canned-cycle torture test across all 3 planes) run clean. I also hand-verified the G92 offset math against the spec's own numeric example.

**Bug-hunting:** I ran two rounds of independent adversarial code review (fresh agents re-reading the spec against the code) plus my own testing, which caught and fixed 9 real bugs, including: the spindle modal-group field never syncing with M3/M4/M5, M2/M30 incorrectly wiping G92 offset parameters, a state mutation happening before validation (corrupting error-exit output), a sign inversion in the cutter-comp entry-move geometry, a corner-arc convexity sign inversion, cutter-comp corner arcs being stepped as separate sub-motions instead of one continuous path (a literal spec requirement), a dwell sharing a line with motion not contributing to cumulative trace time, and arithmetic overflow in expressions leaking as an internal error (exit 2) instead of a program error (exit 1).
